title: Initial continuous RAW editing — Nikon Z6 and Fujifilm X100VI
objective: Deliver continuously editable, non-destructive RAW recipes for the original Nikon Z6 and Fujifilm X100VI, with verified source preservation, retained processing precision, neutral development, exposure/white balance, existing composition/history and shared UI/API behavior. Integrate explicit JPEG output only through the separately delivered exporter.
context_summary: Planning only. The owner explicitly requires ongoing RAW editing like Lightroom's workflow, not WB/exposure conversion into JPEG for later editing. Current code is M4/Develop plus content-space/orientation changes; sources/rendering are byte sRGB and import/cache-miss decode still runs on the owner. No real RAW benchmarks or modes were qualified during planning. Exact modes/firmware remain unknown. LibRaw is the first unpacking candidate; production demosaic/color/precision is a separate evidence and decision gate. JPEG Basic Slice A then B retains the owner-selected next priority, but is not implemented; RAW scheduling does not supersede it. Basic/export/Locate/MCP are not assumed delivered. No cross-plan dependencies, migrations, camera-look matching or custom decoder. Ready tasks are preparation after implementation authorization; unresolved consequential decisions remain proposals. TASK-021 additionally requires the named shared exporter outside this plan and does not block A/B editing handoff. Evidence output paths in commands must be fresh; do not delete previous runs.

Classify reduced/cropped NEF, lossy RAF and capture variations independently; keep source bytes unchanged and public/synthetic fixture licensing explicit.

steps: Inspect metadata with a pinned independent reader and compare it with camera settings; record unknown values honestly.
Verify all manifest hashes and source preservation; review sample coverage and permission without committing private content.
expected_results: A usable coverage manifest and authentic local corpus identify what can and cannot be claimed. Missing owner input remains explicit.

The owner requires ongoing RAW recipes, not conversion to a JPEG or byte raster for later editing. Interface proposals must carry high precision through the whole editing stack.
